evidence.quote: The Lynx rabbit, also called the Luchskaninchen rabbit and the Lux rabbit, is a medium-sized rabbit that weighs 2.5–3.2 kg (5.5–7.1 lb).
The Lynx originates from Germany and was created by Karl Hoffmann from Düsseldorf who first exhibited the breed in 1919.
The Jamora rabbit, also called the Dwarf Gangora rabbit, is a long-haired rabbit breed
It is considered a dwarf rabbit.
Their normal weight is 2 kg (4.4 lb), the maximum permissible weight is 2.5 kg (5.5 lb).
It was first bred in the EU and Germany.
It was bred by Dr. Bernhard Thimm from Dornstadt, as well as Barbara Bauerschmidt and Johannes Heldt from Blaustein.
The goal of these breeders was to create a small, long-haired breed of rabbits that stood out for their appearance.
The Jamora rabbit was shown for the first time in 1990 in Nuremberg.
The recognition by the Central Association of German Rabbit Breeders took place in 1994.
The Perlfee rabbit is a rare breed originating in Germany [disputed – discuss]
They are only found in blueish-grey colour, with dark, light and medium shades accepted, medium is preferred, the belly and around the eyes should be lighter in colour.
It is a recognized breed by the British Rabbit Council but not the American Rabbit Breeders Association.
Perlfee rabbits are rather docile and friendly.
They are lively rabbits who make excellent pets for the beginner.
The Blue of Ham, also known as the Blue of Hem or Bleu de Ham, is a rare breed of domestic rabbit that originated in the Belgian village of Ham-sur-Heure in Wallonia.

evidence.value: viande et fourrure, 1897, Horemans; rare après la WWII
evidence.quote: Developed as a meat and fur breed in 1897 by Ulysses Horemans (who introduced the breed to St. Petersburg in 1902), the once-popular Blue of Ham became rare following World War II.
This rabbit has a "long, dense, silky and lustrous" coat that is slate blue with a blue sub-color, extending as deep as possible.
The Blue of Ham weighs 9.9–13.2 pounds (4.5–6 kg) and is said to be "very sociable".
The Liptov Baldspotted Rabbit (Slovak: Liptovský lysko) is a Slovak breed of domestic rabbit.
It was officially recognized in 2005.
It weighs approximately 4–4.25 kilograms (8.8–9.4 lb).
There are three colour varieties: agouti, blue-agouti, and black.

evidence.value: liste blanche, pas d'autre marque blanche
evidence.quote: The pattern on the head is a white blaze (similar to "Dutch" head markings), but there are no other white markings anywhere on the rabbit.
It has been bred in the Liptov region of Slovakia.
The Carmagnola Grey rabbit is a rare breed from Italy, almost extinct.
It is a large chinchilla-colored breed bred for meat.
The coat of the Carmagnola Grey exhibits chinchilla coloration.
The average weight of an adult Carmagnola Grey is 7.7–9.9 pounds (3.5–4.5 kg).
Fewer than 500 specimens were found in a 2002 population study.
Brazilian domestic rabbit is a medium-sized hardy breed originated in Brazil.
They were developed as a meat breed.
The breed is not current recognized by the American Rabbit Breeders Association or the British Rabbit council.

evidence.value: taille moyenne, fourrure longue et dense
evidence.quote: The Cashmere Lop rabbit is a medium-sized rabbit with long dense fur.
There is also a Miniature Cashmere Lop.

evidence.value: distinct du Dwarf Lop par le BRC, années 1980
evidence.quote: The Cashmere lop was recognised as being different from the Dwarf Lop by the British Rabbit Council in the 1980s.
This breed, which originated in England, comes in many different colors and weighs approximately 4-5 lbs.
The Enderby Island Rabbit, or simply Enderby rabbit or Enderby, is a rare breed of domesticated European rabbit (Oryctolagus cuniculus).
It originates from rabbits introduced to Enderby Island, an uninhabited subantarctic island in New Zealand's Auckland Islands group, from Australia in October 1865 to serve as castaway food.
Enderby Island Rabbits are mainly silver-grey in colour, with an undercoat of dark slate-blue.
Adult rabbits weigh about 2 kg.

evidence.value: naissent noirs ou crème, tiquetage argenté à la puberté
evidence.quote: Kits are born black or cream then silver ticking develops at puberty.
The Swedish Hare, formerly the Elfin rabbit, is a small rabbit weighing 2.3 kg (5 lb).
The breed comes in white, brown, black, grey, and many others.
It was developed in 2008 by Mirjam Gille and Linda Ahlsen in Sweden for its competitive jumping ability.
Český černopesíkatý (Ččp) je české národní plemeno králíka, které vyšlechtil v roce 1974 František Provazník z Holic.
Uznané bylo v roce 1976.
Patří mezi malá plemena, s hmotností 2,00–3,25 kg.
Barva srsti je bílá se šedopopelavým nádechem.
Zbarvením má připomínat polární lišku.
Le lapin bélier, ou lope, est une variété de lapin domestique, se distinguant principalement des autres par ses oreilles tombantes.
le petit bélier est originaire d'Allemagne. Son poids varie entre 2,6 et 3,5 kg ;
The Hulstlander is a small/medium breed of rabbit only recognised in white with pale blue eyes. Any other colour is a fault.

evidence.value: race bovine de petite taille, Corée, aussi Coréenne brune
evidence.quote: La hanu (coréen : 한우), également nommée Coréenne brune, est une race bovine de petite taille, originaire de Corée.
Elle était autrefois utilisée comme animal de trait, mais cet usage a pratiquement disparu.
Elle est désormais élevée principalement pour la viande.

evidence.quote: D'après la base de données DAD-IS, les femelles toisent en moyenne 1,17 m pour 355 kg, et les mâles 1,24 m pour 466 kg.
